correctness.rationale: Signed-generator maximizers suffice by strict convexity of squared Euclidean norm; central symmetry proves unique center zero. For orientation imbalance b_v, the exact objective is sum_v(|b_v|+t)^2. An even unicyclic graph has exactly two globally pure source/sink orientations, giving the degree bound with two contacts. An odd cycle forces a mixed cycle vertex with loss at least 4(d_v+t-1), so total deficit >=4(delta_C+t-1). Explicit orientations with one minimum-degree cycle defect attain equality. A unique defect and the alternating cycle plus independent defect choice yield exactly 4k_C distinct contacts. The proof covers all finite unicyclic graphs and real t>0. Exact standalone package verifier passed 8,490 canonical graph/parameter max-and-contact checks and 216 full sign-endpoint checks; these finite tests corroborate but do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The result exactly classifies Euclidean circumradius, unique center, all supporting vertices and every diametral pair of a natural infinitely parameterized family of newly introduced convex bodies. A single odd cycle forces a precise, quantified radial loss determined by the minimum cycle degree, while all even-cycle cases attain the vertexwise bound. The sharp contact count jumps from 2 to 4k_C and continues to hold under arbitrary tree attachments and a continuum of coordinate box sizes t>0; this is a structural family classification rather than a small instance or generic symmetric-body bound.
